text: Radioactive iodine's long-term effect on thyroid function and size in non-toxic multinodular goitre was studied in 69 patients with growing goitre causing compression symptoms or cosmetic inconvenience (chosen for high operative risk, prior thyroidectomy, or surgery refusal), followed ≥12 months (median 48). Intended dose: 3.7 MBq/g thyroid tissue corrected to 100% iodine-131 uptake at 24 hours. Fifty-six received one dose, 12 two, one four. In 45 single-dose euthyroid patients, median thyroid volume fell from 73 (IQR 50–106) ml to 29 (23–48) ml at 24 months (39 measured); median reduction 40 (22–48) ml (60%, p<0.0001), half within three months. Two-dose, hypothyroid and hyperthyroid patients also showed significant reduction. Eleven developed hypothyroidism (five-year risk 22%, 95% CI 4.8–38.4%). Side effects were few (three hyperthyroidism, two radiation thyroiditis); one patient was dissatisfied and referred for operation. Radioactive iodine is an attractive alternative to surgery in selected cases.
